title: Pappardelle with Slow-Braised Beef Ragù
summary: Wide fresh egg pappardelle tossed in butter and Parmesan, topped with a deeply savoury beef ragù braised low and slow until it falls apart.
equipment: large ovenproof casserole with lid (at least 4 litres)

ingredients.item: boneless beef chuck, cut into 5 cm chunks
fine sea salt or table salt
tin whole plum tomatoes, crushed by hand

ingredients.note: shop-bought, or the fresh egg dough cut 2.5 cm wide

ingredients.item: fine salt for 4 litres of pasta water (0.8%)
ingredients.note: about 5.25 tsp; most of it goes down the drain

ingredients.item: Parmesan-style hard cheese (microbial rennet), finely grated

steps.title: Season the beef
steps.text: Pat the beef chunks dry and season all over with the salt and pepper. Preheat the oven to 160°C (140°C fan) at least 20 minutes ahead, so it's fully up to temperature before the casserole goes in.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Heat the olive oil in a large ovenproof casserole over medium-high heat and brown the beef in two batches, 4-5 minutes per batch, until deeply coloured on two or three sides. Browning in batches matters here - crowding the pan would trap steam and stop the meat catching colour, and it's that colour that gives the ragù its roasted depth. Set the browned beef aside on a plate.

steps.title: Build the vegetable base
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium and add the onion, carrot and celery to the same pot, scraping up the browned bits stuck to the bottom as they soften over 6-8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, tomato purée, rosemary and sage and cook for 2 minutes more, just until fragrant.

steps.title: Braise the ragù
steps.text: Add the crushed tomatoes and water, then return the beef and its juices to the pot and bring everything to a gentle simmer. Cover and transfer to the oven to braise for 3-3½ hours, stirring once or twice, until the beef falls apart easily when pressed with a spoon. Long, gentle heat is what melts the connective tissue in chuck into gelatine, and that's what gives the sauce its silky body.

steps.title: Shred and reduce
steps.text: Lift out and discard the herb sprigs, then shred the beef right in the pot using two forks. If the sauce looks thin, simmer it uncovered on the hob for 10-15 minutes until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon. Taste and adjust the salt before setting it aside.

steps.title: Cook the pappardelle
steps.text: Bring 4 litres of water to the boil with the 32 g salt and cook the pappardelle for 2-3 minutes, as fresh egg pasta cooks much faster than dried. Reserve 240 ml of the cooking water before draining.

steps.title: Toss the pasta
steps.text: Lift the pappardelle into a warm pan with the butter, half the Parmesan and 80 ml of the reserved water. Toss until the strands look glossy and lightly coated - the starchy water and melting butter form a light emulsion that clings to the pasta rather than pooling underneath it.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Divide the buttered pappardelle between warm plates, spoon the ragù generously over the top, and finish with the remaining Parmesan and the orange zest if using. Serve at once while everything is hot.

tips: Don't skip the batch-browning of the beef - crowding the pan is the most common way to lose that roasted depth, since the meat steams rather than caramelises.
Chuck is ready when a chunk breaks apart with gentle pressure from a spoon; if it still resists, give it another 30 minutes, as it softens suddenly near the end.
If the ragù tastes flat after braising, a final uncovered reduction on the hob concentrates the flavour far more effectively than extra salt.
Toss the pasta with butter and water first, and add the Parmesan only once it's off the direct heat, so the cheese melts smoothly instead of clumping.
storage: The ragù keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days, or can be frozen for up to 3 months; thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently until piping hot (74°C) throughout before serving. Fresh pappardelle is best cooked and eaten the same day rather than stored dressed, as it softens quickly once sauced. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
